status.en: 10 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Rumbek, Juba and Abyei.
status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Rumbek, Juba og Abyei.

summary.en: Sudanese armed forces have continued drone strikes on markets in the disputed Abyei border region, killing more than 150 people in each attack. Communal clashes persist, with SSPDF and SPLA-IO forces fighting in Kapoeta North, Eastern Equatoria, and in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, while a separate ambush killed two people in Kajo-Keji County. Monitors warned of rising violence ahead of December elections and reported 40,000 people displaced by renewed Upper Nile fighting. The UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den sudanske hæren har fortsatt droneangrep på markeder i den omstridte grensen mot Abyei, og har drept mer enn 150 personer i hvert angrep. Kommunale sammenstøt vedvarer, med SSPDF- og SPLA-IO-styrker som kjemper i Kapoeta North i Øst-Equatoria, og i Wij-Panyikang i Øvre Nilen, mens et separat bakholdsangrep drepte to personer i Kajo-Keji fylke. Observatører advarte om økende vold før desembervalg og rapporterte at 40 000 personer er fordrevet på grunn av fornyet kamp i Øvre Nilen. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
